all_articles.html:
Chapter 4 Exercises

From: Finite Difference Methods for Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations, R. J. LeVeque, SIAM, 2007. https://faculty.washington.edu/rjl/fdmbook/

Exercise 4.1 (Convergence of SOR)

The m-file iter_bvp_Asplit.m implements the Jacobi, Gauss-Seidel, and SOR matrix splitting methods on the linear system arising from the boundary value problem u''(x) = f(x) in one space dimension.

  1. Run this program for each method and produce a plot similar to Figure 4.2.

  2. The convergence behavior of SOR is very sensitive to the choice of \omega (omega in the code). Try changing from the optimal \omega to \omega = 1.8 or 1.95.

  3. Let g(\omega) = \rho(G(\omega)) be the spectral radius of the iteration matrix G for a given value of \omega. Write a program to produce a plot of g(\omega) for 0\leq \omega \leq 2.

  4. From equations (4.22) one might be tempted to try to implement SOR as

         for iter=1:maxiter
        uGS = (DA - LA) \ (UA*u + rhs);
        u = u + omega * (uGS - u);
        end

    where the matrices have been defined as in iter_bvp_Asplit.m. Try this computationally and observe that it does not work well. Explain what is wrong with this and derive the correct expression (4.24).

Exercise 4.2 (Forward vs. backward Gauss-Seidel)

  1. The Gauss-Seidel method for the discretization of u''(x) = f(x) takes the form (4.5) if we assume we are marching forwards across the grid, for i=1,~2,~\ldots,~m. We can also define a backwards Gauss-Seidel method by setting

    \tag{Ex4.2a} u_i^{[k+1]} = \frac{1}{2} (u_{i-1}^{[k]} + u_{i+1}^{[k+1]} - h^2 f_i), \qquad \text{for}~ i = m,~m-1,~m-2,~\ldots,~1.

    Show that this is a matrix splitting method of the type described in Section 4.2 with M = D-U and N=L.

  2. Implement this method in iter_bvp_Asplit.m and observe that it converges at the same rate as forward Gauss-Siedel for this problem.

  3. Modify the code so that it solves the boundary value problem

    \tag{Ex4.2b} \epsilon u''(x) = au'(x) + f(x),\qquad 0\leq x \leq 1,

    with u(0) = 0 and u(1) = 0, where a\geq 0 and the u'(x_i) term is discretized by the one-sided approximation (U_i - U_{i-1})/h. Test both forward and backward Gauss-Seidel for the resulting linear system. With a=1 and \epsilon = 0.0005. You should find that they behave very differently:

    Explain intuitively why sweeping in one direction works so much better than in the other.

    Hint: Note that this equation is the steady equation for an advection-diffusion PDE u_t(x,t) + au_x(x,t) = \epsilon u_{xx}(x,t) - f(x). You might consider how the methods behave in the case \epsilon = 0.
